title: Claiming a fulfilled request only checks that a rate limit exists, so de-listing a venue by zeroing its limit would trap pending funds
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.5.2.2 describes the gate on claiming a fulfilled deposit: "This is an **existence check only**: it requires the `LIMIT_7540_DEPOSIT` rate limit keyed to the `token` to have a non-zero `maxAmount`, reverting otherwise, and it **neither decreases nor increases** the available amount. This confirms the vault is whitelisted before shares are claimed." A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.5.4.2 says the same for claiming a redemption, and the Centrifuge cancel/claim operations (A...2.6.1.2 through A...2.6.4.2) use the identical `rateLimitExists` pattern, reverting with `invalid-action`.

Not charging the claim is correct: the allowance was already consumed when the request was submitted, so charging again would double-count the same exposure.

But the existence check has a consequence the Artifact does not draw out. Because the whitelist **is** the rate limit (A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.2.1.2), the way to revoke a venue is to zero its `maxAmount`. Doing so while a request is pending would make the claim revert — the assets have already left the proxy, the entitlement exists at the vault, and the function that retrieves it is gated on a limit that has just been set to zero.

That is a real operational hazard rather than a theoretical one, because the async positions are precisely the RWA vaults whose fulfilment takes days. Revoking a counterparty mid-flight is exactly the moment someone would want to, and it is the moment the mechanism turns against the holder.

The safe sequence it implies: never zero a limit until pending requests are claimed or cancelled. Nothing in the specification enforces that ordering, so it is an unwritten operational precondition on a governance action.
description: Claim operations run an existence check requiring non-zero maxAmount and neither decrease nor increase the allowance — the charge happened at request time, but the gate still blocks on a zeroed limit.
